full_target:
Let \(p\) be any prime, \(K\) any field of characteristic \(p\), and
\(\lambda\) an integer with \(0\leq\lambda<p\).
Let \(V(\lambda)\) be the complex irreducible highest-weight
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)\)-module of highest weight \(\lambda\),
of dimension \(\lambda+1\). Its Chevalley generators satisfy

\[
[h,x]=2x,\qquad[h,y]=-2y,\qquad[x,y]=h.
\]

Choose a nonzero highest-weight vector \(v\) with \(xv=0\) and
\(hv=\lambda v\). Let \(U_{\mathbb Z}\) be the integer subalgebra of
the universal enveloping algebra generated by all divided powers
\(X_r=x^r/r!\), \(Y_r=y^r/r!\), for integers \(r\geq0\).
An **admissible lattice** \(M\subset V(\lambda)\) is a free abelian
subgroup with an integer basis that is also a complex basis, stable under
\(U_{\mathbb Z}\). It is arbitrary, not necessarily the minimal lattice.

Put \(V(K)=M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\). The Lie algebra
\(L(K)=(\mathbb Zx+\mathbb Zy+\mathbb Zh)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}K\)
acts by the induced lattice operators. This is the Chevalley
\(\mathfrak{sl}_2\) construction also in characteristic 2.
Prove that \(V(K)\) is nonzero and every \(K\)-linear subspace
invariant under \(x,y,h\) is zero or all of \(V(K)\).
Both \(\lambda=0\) and \(p=2\) are included; \(K\) need not be
algebraically closed.

dependencies.statement: For every complex vector space V, every index type I, endomorphism f, injective eigenvalue family μ:I→ℂ, and family a:I→V of nonzero f-eigenvectors with f(a_i)=μ_i a_i, the family a is complex-linearly independent.

lean.type: ∀ (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V] (ι : Type w) (f : Module.End ℂ V) (μ : ι → ℂ) (a : ι → V), Function.Injective μ → (∀ i, f.HasEigenvector (μ i) (a i)) → LinearIndependent ℂ a
lean.proof:
intro V _ _ ι f μ a hμ ha
exact f.eigenvectors_linearIndependent' μ hμ a ha

dependencies.justification: Specialize the inspected domain/torsion-free theorem to ℂ, preserving arbitrary index type and vector space. Fields supply domain and torsion-free instances. Consumer R001 proves the weight family injective and each vector nonzero by characteristic-zero commutator induction; this result is never applied to reduced weights.

dependencies.statement: For every field K, finite-dimensional K-vector space V, natural n, and independent family a:Fin n→V with dim_K V=n, the K-linear span of the range of a is all V.

lean.type: ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [FiniteDimensional K V] (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → V), Module.finrank K V = n → LinearIndependent K a → Submodule.span K (Set.range a) = ⊤

intro K _ V _ _ _ n a hd hi

dependencies.justification: Specialize the inspected division-ring theorem to a field and Fin n, reverse the given dimension equality and simplify Fintype.card (Fin n). Used by R001 to complete the characteristic-zero basis and R005 to span the invariant subspace's constructed independent vectors.

proof: Write m=λ as a natural number, N=m+1 and I={0,...,m}. All occurrences of factorials in complex formulas mean their integer images in C. We retain the original arbitrary admissible lattice M. 1. Characteristic-zero coordinates. From [h,y]=-2y, induction gives h(y^i v)=(m-2i)y^i v. From [x,y]=h and xv=0, induction gives x(y^i v)=i(m-i+1)y^(i-1)v for i≥1. Iterating shows x^i y^i v=i!·m(m-1)...(m-i+1)v≠0 for i≤m. Consequently e_i=y^i v/i! is nonzero. A relation among these distinct h-eigenvectors is separated by applying ∏_{k≠j}(h-(m-2k)Id); its coefficient multiplier is a product of nonzero complex numbers. Thus they are independent, and their cardinality dim_C V=N makes them a basis. The vector y^(m+1)v has eigenvalue -m-2, which is absent from this basis; expanding it in the basis shows it is zero. Hence xe_0=0, xe_i=(m-i+1)e_(i-1), ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) below m, ye_m=0. Iterating and dividing factorials gives X_r e_i=choose(m-i+r,r)e_(i-r) for r≤i and zero otherwise, and Y_r e_i=choose(i+r,r)e_(i+r) when i+r≤m and zero otherwise. 2. Integral scaled matrix units. Put P0=Y_m X_m and T_ij=X_(m-i) P0 Y_(m-j). Evaluation on each e_k shows P0=E_mm, X_(m-i)P0=E_im, and P0 Y_(m-j)=choose(m,j)E_mj. Thus T_ij=choose(m,j)E_ij. Set q_j=j!(m-j)! and D=m!. The factorial identity q_j choose(m,j)=D shows that S_ij=q_j T_ij=D E_ij. Every S_ij preserves M: all divided powers do by admissibility, and q_j is an integer. Restrict S_ij to Z-linear endomorphisms of M. The equalities S_ij S_kl=δ_jk D S_il and Σ_i S_ii=D Id hold in V by the matrix-unit calculation, and hence on M because its inclusion into V is injective. Also r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r on M for all r. No localization and no claim about rational ranks of submodules of C is needed. 3. Base change. For clarity identify the target M⊗_Z K with K⊗_Z M by the canonical flip m⊗a↦a⊗m. Its inverse is the reverse flip; the balanced tensor relations show they are inverse K-linear maps. The original integer basis of M, indexed by I, base changes to a K-basis of K⊗_Z M, so its K-dimension is N>0. Each Z-linear map A of M induces the K-linear map A_K with A_K(a⊗u)=a⊗A(u). Addition, composition and integer scalar multiplication commute with this operation: verify on pure tensors, which span the tensor product. Applying this to the preceding integral identities yields the same equations over K, with D replaced by d=(m!:K). 4. Invertibility and invariant subspaces. Since m

propositions.statement: Let p be any prime, K any field of characteristic p, λ an integer with 0≤λ<p, V=V(λ) the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂-module of dimension λ+1, and x,y,h its Chevalley operators satisfying hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h. Let v∈V be nonzero with xv=0 and hv=λv. Let U_ℤ be the integer enveloping subalgebra generated by all X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r!, r≥0. Let M⊆V be any U_ℤ-stable free abelian subgroup with an integer basis also a complex basis of V. The target space is M⊗_ℤ K with the induced x,y,h actions and the Chevalley Lie algebra (ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, including characteristic two.

For every natural m, complex vector space V of dimension m+1, endomorphisms x,y,h with hx−xh=2x, hy−yh=−2y, xy−yx=h, and nonzero v with xv=0 and hv=mv, the vectors e_i=y^i v/i!, 0≤i≤m, form a complex basis. They satisfy xe_0=0, xe_i=(m−i+1)e_(i−1) for 1≤i≤m, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<m, ye_m=0 and he_i=(m−2i)e_i. For all r≥0, X_r=x^r/r! sends e_i to choose(m−i+r,r)e_(i−r) if r≤i and to zero otherwise; Y_r=y^r/r! sends e_i to choose(i+r,r)e_(i+r) if i+r≤m and to zero otherwise.

For every natural m, complex vector space V with basis e_0,…,e_m and divided powers X_r=x^r/r!,Y_r=y^r/r! having the action formulas in the following explicit form: X_r e_i=choose(m−i+r,r)e_(i−r) for r≤i and zero otherwise, Y_r e_i=choose(i+r,r)e_(i+r) for i+r≤m and zero otherwise, let M⊆V be any integer submodule preserved by all X_r,Y_r. Put D=m!, q_j=j!(m−j)!, T_ij=X_(m−i)Y_m X_m Y_(m−j) and s_ij=(q_j T_ij)|M. Then s_ij∈End_ℤ M, s_ij s_kl=δ_jk D s_il, and Σ_(i=0)^m s_ii=D Id_M. For every r≥0 the restrictions satisfy r!(X_r|M)=(x|M)^r and r!(Y_r|M)=(y|M)^r. Here x=X_1,y=Y_1, multiplication is composition with right factor first, and δ_jk is 1 if j=k and 0 otherwise.

For every natural m, abelian group M with an integer basis b_0,…,b_m, and field K, the space K⊗_ℤ M has basis 1⊗b_0,…,1⊗b_m and dimension m+1, and is nonzero. The tensor flip m⊗a↦a⊗m identifies M⊗_ℤ K, equipped with its K-action on the second factor, K-linearly with K⊗_ℤ M. For every integer endomorphism f of M this flip intertwines f⊗Id_K with Id_K⊗f.

For every prime p, field K of characteristic p, natural m<p, integer module M, endomorphisms x,y∈End_ℤ M and sequences A_r,B_r∈End_ℤ M with A_1=x, B_1=y, r!A_r=x^r and r!B_r=y^r, suppose the endomorphisms s_ij=j!(m−j)! A_(m−i) B_m A_m B_(m−j), indexed by 0≤i,j≤m, satisfy s_ij s_kl=δ_jk m! s_il and Σ_i s_ii=m! Id_M. On K⊗_ℤ M let Φ(f)(a⊗u)=a⊗f(u), d=(m!:K), and U_ij=d⁻¹Φ(s_ij). Then d≠0, U_ij U_kl=δ_jk U_il and Σ_i U_ii=Id. Every K-subspace preserved by Φ(x) and Φ(y) is preserved by all U_ij. The conclusion applies when m=0, and requires no algebraic closure or reduced-weight distinctness.

For every field K, positive natural N, finite-dimensional K-vector space Q with dim_K Q=N, and endomorphisms U_ij indexed by Fin N satisfying U_ij U_kl=δ_jk U_il and Σ_i U_ii=Id_Q, every K-linear subspace W⊆Q preserved by all U_ij is zero or all Q. Multiplication is composition with the right factor acting first.

replacements.original_dependency: Distinct-eigenvector independence and dimension-to-basis arguments in characteristic zero
replacements.explanation: Use inspected general eigenvector independence and span-by-cardinality results after the explicit commutator inductions. Do not impose IsSl2Triple's h≠0 condition; λ=0 remains included.

replacements.original_dependency: Localization R=ℤ_(p), M_R, equality of coordinate modules J_i, rank calculation n=nr, injectivity of ℚ⊗_R J→ℂ, and DVR generation J=Rb
replacements.explanation: Delete this entire lattice-classification route. N002 proves s_ij=λ!E_ij in complex coordinates but restricts only the integral s_ij and their polynomial identities to M. B004 transports these identities directly to K⊗M, B003/B006 give its dimension from the original integer basis, and N005 proves simplicity by constructing an independent family in any nonzero invariant subspace.

replacements.original_dependency: Invertibility of each binomial coefficient choose(λ,j) in ℤ_(p) and reduction of the localized standard-form lattice
replacements.explanation: Multiply T_ij by j!(λ−j)! to obtain a common scale D=λ!. Only D and r! for r≤λ need invert in K; B005 gives these units. B004 transfers integer identities before normalization, without localization or an embedding K→ℂ.
